body.statement: Whenever \(\mathcal M_{T_0,T_1}(0)\ne\varnothing\), for every nonempty stratum with \(0\le\gamma\le\kappa_\star/2\), \(R_{\mathrm{or}}(\gamma)\asymp R_{\mathrm{ad}}(\gamma)\asymp\rho_{\mathrm{ad}}(\gamma)\), uniformly in \(T_0,T_1\). Thus global honesty imposes no rate adaptation penalty throughout the weak-decoding half of the attainable margin range.
body.justification: The theorem rules out the tempting but false claim that the unidentified boundary automatically creates an adaptation tax on every positive stratum.
body.gap: CaiLow2004 and NicklVanDeGeer2013 show that honesty may obstruct adaptation on other unions; the loading-margin union instead has an exact no-penalty region that requires same-stratum compensated rotations.
body.consumer: It tells users with weak estimated decoding geometry that supplying an external lower margin bound cannot improve the achievable order of interval width.
